rationale: This is a monotone re-ranking of the archive's existing "Obligation-Netted Fundamental To Price" with WINSOR swapped for IND_RANK — a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the stated goal (diagnosing whether the alpha is tail-driven) is a robustness check, not a new hypothesis.

target_name: Net Cash Cheapness With Real Gross Profit
rationale: The net-cash-to-price valuation leg is a genuinely different balance-sheet channel from the earnings- and book-based legs already tested and the conditioning story is coherent with monotone non-negative ranks, though the product will likely be dominated by the well-documented gross profitability leg, so the incremental content over Novy-Marx is uncertain.

This is a near-duplicate of the archive's failed "Weakest-Link Cheap And Profitable" — same MIN-of-two-ranks construction with ib+dp→ebitda and oancf/at→oancf/lt substituted — so it re-tests an already-rejected conjunctive design with a highly correlated coverage proxy.

The persistence-count formulation of accrual conservatism is a legitimately novel quality state distinct from the level-based accruals anomaly, but the reasoning is internally wrong — a zero count collapses the product to exactly zero for a potentially large mass of firms, destroying the valuation ordering there — so the construction is less continuous than claimed.

The short-side framing and liabilities-to-price valuation leg are a reasonable economic complement to the long-side proposals and the sign is internally consistent, but the construct is close to the published distress anomaly and liabilities-to-price is mechanically correlated with book-to-market, whose unconditional sign runs opposite to the expectation.

This is the third instance of the same MUL(IND_RANK cheap yield, IND_RANK margin-dynamics) template already tried unsuccessfully in the archive with only the quality leg swapped (trend/level → volatility), and a five-observation annual VOL is a very noisy stability estimate; it also cites a "volatility-deflated yield" predecessor not present in the archive.
